title: The Torture, The Cross, and The Tomb
paragraphs: §The Thorn Crown of the King

So Pilate took Jesus and had him whipped. The soldiers braided a crown from thorns and set it on his head, threw a purple robe over him, and came up to him saying, "Hail, King of the Jews!" Then they greeted him with slaps to the face.

Pilate went back out again and said to them, "I'm presenting him to you, but I want you to know I don't find him guilty of any crime." Just then Jesus came out, wearing the thorn crown and the purple robe. Pilate announced, "Here he is: the Man."
When the high priests and police saw him, they shouted wildly, "Crucify! Crucify!" Pilate told them, "You take him. You crucify him. I find nothing wrong with him."
The Jews answered, "We have a law, and by that law he must die, because he claimed to be the Son of God."
When Pilate heard this, he got even more scared. He went back into the palace and said to Jesus, "Where did you come from?" Jesus gave no answer.
Pilate said, "You won't talk? Don't you know I have the authority to pardon you, and the authority to—crucify you?"
Jesus said, "You don't have a shred of authority over me except what's been given to you from above. That's why the one who handed me over to you has committed a far greater wrong."
At this, Pilate tried hard to set him free, but the Jews shouted him down: "If you let this man go, you're no friend of Caesar's. Anyone who sets himself up as 'king' defies Caesar."

When Pilate heard those words, he led Jesus outside. He sat down at the judgment seat in the area called Stone Court (in Hebrew, Gabbatha). It was the preparation day for Passover. The hour was noon. Pilate said to the Jews, "Here is your king."
They shouted back, "Kill him! Kill him! Crucify him!" Pilate said, "Am I supposed to crucify your king?" The high priests answered, "We have no king except Caesar."

Pilate gave in to their demand. He handed him over to be crucified. They took Jesus away. Carrying his cross, Jesus went out to the place called Skull Hill (in Hebrew, Golgotha), where they crucified him—and with him two others, one on each side, Jesus in the middle. Pilate wrote a sign and had it put on the cross. It read: jesus the nazarene the king of the jews.
§The Crucifixion

Many of the Jews read the sign, because the place where Jesus was crucified was right next to the city. It was written in Hebrew, Latin, and Greek. The Jewish high priests objected. "Don't write," they said to Pilate, "'The King of the Jews.' Write, 'This man said, "I am the King of the Jews."'"
Pilate said, "What I've written, I've written."

When they crucified him, the Roman soldiers took his clothes and divided them four ways—a fourth to each soldier. But his robe was seamless, a single piece of weaving, so they said to each other, "Let's not tear it. Let's throw dice to see who gets it." This confirmed the Scripture that said, "They divided my clothes among them and threw dice for my coat." (The soldiers proved the Scriptures right!)

While the soldiers were looking after themselves, Jesus' mother, his aunt, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene stood at the foot of the cross. Jesus saw his mother and the disciple he loved standing near her. He said to his mother, "Woman, here is your son." Then to the disciple, "Here is your mother." From that moment the disciple took her as his own mother.
Jesus, seeing that everything had been finished, so that the Scripture record would also be complete, then said, "I'm thirsty."

A jug of sour wine was standing nearby. Someone put a sponge soaked with the wine on a javelin and lifted it to his mouth. After he took the wine, Jesus said, "It's done… finished." Bowing his head, he gave up his spirit.

Then the Jews—since it was the day of Sabbath preparation, and they didn't want the bodies to stay on the crosses over the Sabbath (it was a high holy day that year)—asked Pilate to have their legs broken to speed up death, and the bodies taken down. So the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first man crucified with Jesus, and then the other. When they got to Jesus, they saw he was already dead, so they didn't break his legs. One of the soldiers stabbed him in the side with his spear. Blood and water poured out.
The eyewitness to these events has given an accurate report. He saw it himself and is telling the truth, so that you, too, will believe.
These things happened to confirm the Scripture: "Not a bone in his body was broken," and the other Scripture that reads, "They will stare at the one they pierced."

After all this, Joseph of Arimathea (he was a disciple of Jesus, but secretly, because he was afraid of the Jews) asked Pilate for Jesus' body. Pilate gave permission. So Joseph came and took the body.

Nicodemus, who had first come to Jesus at night, now came in broad daylight, carrying a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about seventy-five pounds. They took Jesus' body and, following the Jewish burial custom, wrapped it in linen with the spices. There was a garden near the place where he was crucified, and in the garden a new tomb in which no one had ever been placed. So, because it was Sabbath preparation for the Jews and the tomb was close by, they laid Jesus in it.
